histories: A former dock guard who enlisted for regular wages. He keeps his boots polished even in the island mud.
A cooper's son who knows how a sound barrel should ring. He counts supply casks before he counts enemy flags.
He learned to read from discarded shipping notices. He still saves every letter that reaches the garrison.
He came aboard as a cook's helper and stayed for a share of the prize money. He can stretch a pot of stew remarkably far.
A former ferry hand who knows the price of a broken rope. He checks his knots twice and his captain's promises three times.
He once repaired fishing nets for a living. He wants enough gold to own a boat whose course is his to choose.
Before the shrine, he copied cargo tallies. He still writes numbers in the margins of his prayers.
He used to mend lamps along the waterfront. Since the dreams began, he cannot sleep beside an unlit wick.
He followed a missing brother's trail to the shrine. He remembers the search more clearly than what he found.
